_source: Started as a transcription (not a capture) from two community Linux
projects that speak to Pulsar's Nordic wireless dongle:
packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux (drivers/nordic.py, an address-mapped
memory protocol for VID 0x3554) and andrewrabert/python-pulsar-mouse-tool,
its credited source. That gave the packet shape (17 bytes, opcode +
address + length, sum8_minus_55 checksum) but not this exact model's IDs.
Confirmed since, statically, by running tools/analyze-driver.py against
the real Pulsar Fusion Windows installer (innoextract'd, then pointed at
'Pulsar Fusion Wireless Mice.exe' and the Cfg.ini it ships) -- no
hardware capture, but real vendor source, not a secondhand description:
- Cfg.ini's [OPT] section: VID=25A7,3554  PID=fa7b,f507  PID2=fa7c,f508,f509
-- matches the 3554:f507/f509 this project already found live via
`hskctl probe` on real hardware, and adds a second vendor id (25a7,
presumably an older USB bridge chip revision, same pattern as
G-Wolves shipping several PIDs across hardware revisions) this
project has no hardware to confirm.
- Cfg.ini's [DEV_13] is this exact model: Name=X2H Mini Wireless,
CID=0x06 (shared by every wireless model in the file -- DEV_1 through
DEV_21 are all CID=0x06, meaning the app treats them as one protocol
family and tells them apart by a model id, MID=0x0D for this one),
Sensor=0x3395 (PixArt PAW3395), DPI=400,800,1600,3200 (four stages
out of the box -- NOT seven like the G-Wolves profile), Debounce=3.
This is capability/default metadata the app's UI uses, not wire-
protocol byte offsets -- it doesn't tell us where MID or the DPI
stages live in a packet, only that they exist and what a fresh X2H
mini ships with.
- The app itself ('Pulsar Fusion Wireless Mice.exe') is native C++/MFC,
not .NET or Electron -- confirmed importing HidD_SetFeature,
HidD_GetHidGuid, HidD_GetPreparsedData, HidP_GetCaps, so the transport
really is HID Feature reports, matching this profile's `transport.kind`.
But native code embeds packet bytes as immediate values in machine
code, not as a labelled blob the way .NET's FieldRVA let this same
script pull G-Wolves' HTS_*_CMD tables out directly -- so the actual
opcode/address bytes below are still the pre-existing transcription,
not decoded from this binary. Getting those needs either real
disassembly of this exe, or a live USB capture while it runs.
Every field below is marked _needsVerification, which hskctl already
treats as a hard stop on writing (see Profile.field_writable) --
exactly the gate `dpiStageCount` and the sleep timer relied on in the
G-Wolves profile before they were confirmed on hardware. Reads are
harmless even if a byte offset here is wrong: HIDIOCGFEATURE cannot
damage the device, it can only come back with a number that is
obviously not a battery percentage. Writes are where a wrong offset
gets expensive, so none are enabled here.
DPI stage values and LED colour are deliberately not mapped: the source
describes them as 4-byte records on the device with their own per-record
checksum (0x55 - value), which this engine's single packet-level
checksum has no hook for. That needs a small protocol.py addition
(a record-level checksum encoding) before it can be done honestly --
see the note on 'dpi_record_nordic' below. Until then this profile
covers battery, firmware version, polling rate, DPI stage count/index,
lift-off distance, debounce, motion sync, angle snap, ripple control,
turbo mode and the sleep timer.
status: partial means hskctl will talk to the device once the PID
matches, but every reading needs sanity-checking against the Pulsar
Fusion app on Windows before anyone trusts it -- and every write stays
refused until _needsVerification is removed field by field.

match._comment: vendorIds/productIds now match Cfg.ini's own [OPT] block from the real Pulsar Fusion installer (VID=25A7,3554  PID=fa7b,f507  PID2=fa7c,f508,f509) as well as what `hskctl probe` found live on real hardware: the cabled mouse enumerates as 3554:f507 (config endpoint on interface 11, vendor usage page 0xff04, feature report id 6 -- the wired probe's top candidate, score 125, fully identified). The RF receiver is a SEPARATE USB device, 3554:f509 ('Pulsar 4K Wireless Receiver') -- its config-endpoint interface has not been captured yet (the probe run so far only showed generic-usage-page interfaces, none of them identified). 25a7:fa7b/fa7c are Cfg.ini's alternate ids (presumably an older USB bridge chip revision) with no hardware here to confirm them against. Do NOT add 0x3710:0x1403 (X2H Wired Medium) to this profile: that model speaks a different, 64-byte, register-addressed protocol (the one x2a.py/x2h.py implement), not the 17-byte memory-mapped one this file describes -- it needs its own profile.

transport._comment: Corrected against the real, cloned source of packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux (not a secondhand summary): drivers/nordic.py and drivers/x2_crazylight.py -- the latter decoded from an actual Pulsar Fusion USB capture (GitHub issue #7), independent of the former -- both agree the transport is a raw USB Output report (SET_REPORT, wValue high byte 0x02) with report id 0x08, read back over the interrupt IN endpoint, NOT a Feature report (HIDIOCGFEATURE/HIDIOCSFEATURE) as first guessed from `hskctl probe`'s feature report id 6 on this interface. hskctl's existing transport.kind: "output" already implements exactly this shape (write_output = os.write, read_input = os.read) with no engine changes needed -- byte 0 of every command template below is now 0x08 to match.

commands._comment: Two shapes here. 'battery'/'version' are their own opcodes (byte 1) with data from byte 2, matching the G-Wolves style. Everything else rides the dongle's memory-mapped get/set (opcode 0x08 read / 0x07 write, at a fixed address baked into each command's template since every hskctl field is its own fixed address, not a runtime parameter) -- byte 3:4 address (endianness unconfirmed, written big-endian here), byte 5 length, value from byte 6.

battery._note: [6]=percent, [7]=power/charging, [8:10]=millivolts per the nordic.py summary. Only percent and charging are mapped here; battery_mv would need a u16 field of its own once confirmed.

pollingRate._note: address 0x00. Raw<->Hz table confirmed from packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux's real source (drivers/nordic.py POLL_HZ_TO_VAL) -- 125/2000/4000/8000 credited there to an actual Pulsar Fusion USB capture (github.com/packerlschupfer/pulsar-mouse-linux issue #7 on the X2 CrazyLight, a different model sharing this same Nordic register map), 250/500/1000 to andrewrabert's earlier tool. The encoding itself (which raw byte means which rate) is solid; which of these seven rates the X2H mini specifically offers in Fusion's UI is not confirmed -- see the field's uiOptions note.

sleep._note: address 0xb7, described as 'units of 10s'; encoded below with scale:10 so the field itself still speaks seconds.

batteryPercent._needsVerification: byte offset transcribed from a summary of nordic.py, not read from source or hardware

firmwareVersion._needsVerification: offset transcribed, not confirmed; major.minor only per the source (no patch byte reported)

pollingRate._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same valueChecksum mechanism, different address) -- read value (1000 Hz) is a plausible real default, not independently cross-checked against Fusion. uiOptions stays the conservative 125/250/500/1000 until 2000/4000/8000 are confirmed reachable on this model.

dpiStageCount._note: Left read-only deliberately, not just unconfirmed: writing DPI stage count wrong is exactly the class of bug that broke DPI writes entirely on the G-Wolves profile until repaired (see gwolves-hsk-pro-4k.json's repairOnWrite). Read value (1) matches the owner's confirmed real single-stage setup.

activeDpiStage._note: Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary. Read value (0) is consistent with the owner's confirmed single active stage. Still 0-based, unlike the G-Wolves profile's 1-based activeDpiStage -- do not compare the two raw.

liftOffDistance._note: Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary. Read value (1mm) is a plausible default, not independently cross-checked.

debounceMs._note: Read value (3) is an EXACT match to the real Pulsar Fusion installer's Cfg.ini [DEV_13] factory default (Debounce=3) for this model. Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary.

motionSync._note: CANARY FIELD: unverified marker deliberately removed first, alone, to test the new valueChecksum write path on real hardware before trusting it for every other field. Confirm `hskctl set motionSync off` then `hskctl get motionSync` (and the reverse) round-trip correctly before removing _needsVerification from anything else in this profile.

angleSnap._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same mechanism, different address).

rippleControl._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same mechanism, different address).

turboMode._note: Write path confirmed on hardware via the motionSync canary (same mechanism, different address).

sleepSeconds._note: Read value (30s) confirmed correct by the owner against their actual mouse's real auto-sleep behavior. Write path confirmed via the motionSync canary.

_followUp: READS AND WRITES BOTH CONFIRMED WORKING on real hardware, cabled, as of this note. Reads: `hskctl status` returns batteryPercent=100, charging=false, firmwareVersion=2.24, pollingRate=1000, dpiStageCount=1 (owner-confirmed real value), activeDpiStage=0, liftOffDistance=1mm, debounceMs=3 (EXACT match to Cfg.ini's [DEV_13] factory default), motionSync/angleSnap=true, rippleControl/turboMode=false, sleepSeconds=30 (owner-confirmed real value). Writes: the per-value checksum this protocol requires (value byte + `0x55 - value` at the next address, alongside the usual whole-packet checksum) is now implemented as a generic `valueChecksum` command-spec option in protocol.py, and round-tripped correctly on real hardware via `hskctl set motionSync off/on` + `hskctl get motionSync` -- read-back matched exactly what was set, both directions. Every scalar field except dpiStageCount (kept read-only on purpose, see its own note) is now writable.

The RF receiver's own config-endpoint interface is still not positively identified for the wireless (dongle) connection -- a fresh `hskctl probe --json` with the dongle connected may score it differently now that all five product ids are in match.productIds and the transport is corrected. Check outputReportIds (not just featureReportIds) in the JSON, since the real transport uses Output reports. Nothing above has been confirmed over the dongle, only cabled.

Two smaller known gaps vs. the real driver, both low risk (neither can corrupt a setting, just occasionally read stale data): autosleep is written to 0xB7 only here, but the real driver mirrors the same value to 0xAD too (ADDR_AUTOSLEEP_ALT) -- needs a 'write to two addresses' hook if the real firmware actually requires both to be in sync. And unsolicited reports (e.g. opcode 0x0A after a profile switch) can desync a naive read-once -- the real driver retries until resp[1] matches the opcode sent; this engine's check_ack only supports a fixed expected byte, not 'echo the sent opcode', so an occasional stale/wrong reply is possible until that's added.

DPI stage values and LED colour still need a record-level checksum (0x55 - value per byte over a 3-4 byte record, not a single value) that protocol.py's new valueChecksum only handles for single-byte values so far -- generalize it (or add a second option) before mapping dpiStage1..N here. Cfg.ini confirms this model ships 4 DPI stages by default (400/800/1600/3200), not 7 like the G-Wolves profile; the real source's _dpi_to_raw/_raw_to_dpi (drivers/nordic.py) is the reference encoding.
pollingRate's uiOptions is deliberately conservative (125/250/500/1000) pending confirmation this model reaches 2000/4000/8000 -- test writing 2000 and see if it takes before widening it.
